title: MFA, Password Policies & Access Keys 🔑
description: Harden your account with multi‑factor authentication and strong credential management.

slides.title: Multi‑Factor Authentication (MFA) 🔐
slides.content:
# Something You Know + Something You Have

MFA adds a second layer of security. Even if someone steals your password, they can’t log in without your MFA device.

AWS supports:
- **Virtual MFA** apps (Google Authenticator, Authy).
- **Hardware MFA** key fob (U2F security keys like YubiKey).
- **SMS text messages** (less secure, but available).

**You must enable MFA on the root account and all IAM users with console access.**

slides.title: Password Policy 🔑
slides.content:
# Enforce Strong Passwords

You can set account‑wide password rules:
- Minimum length (e.g., 8 characters).
- Require uppercase, lowercase, digits, special characters.
- Allow users to change their own passwords.
- Password expiration (e.g., every 90 days).
- Prevent reuse of previous passwords.

These rules are set in **Account Settings** under IAM.

quizData.question: Why is MFA recommended even if you have a very strong password?

options.text: Passwords can be phished, MFA provides a second factor that’s harder to steal remotely

quizData.explanation: Passwords can be compromised via phishing, keyloggers, or data breaches. A physical or app‑based MFA token is much harder for an attacker to obtain.

slides.title: Access Keys: Programmatic Credentials 🗝️
slides.content:
# For CLI and SDK Access

Access keys consist of an **Access Key ID** (public) and a **Secret Access Key** (secret). They’re used by scripts, CLI, and SDKs to sign API calls.

- Create them for IAM users only (not for the root account!).
- Rotate regularly (you can have two active keys simultaneously for seamless rotation).
- Never share them, never commit them to code repositories.
- Use roles instead of keys for EC2 applications.

slides.title: ⚠️ Credential Leaks Are Real
slides.content:
## Guard Keys Like Cash

If a secret key leaks on GitHub, bots will find it in seconds and spin up crypto miners, delete your data, or worse. Use **AWS Secrets Manager** or environment variables, never hard‑code keys.

slides.title: Pro Tip: Use IAM Credential Report 📋
slides.content:
## Audit Your Credentials

The IAM Credential Report (CSV) shows every user, their password age, MFA status, access key rotation, and last used. Download it regularly to spot stale accounts.
